item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Spinner]

Roland’s spinner has three sectors of different colors, orange, purple, and green. Roland spins the pointer 1000 times. The chart below shows how many times the pointer stops on each section.

| Color | Times Stopped |
| :--- | :---: |
| Orange | 510 |
| Purple | 243 |
| Green | 247 |

Draw lines on the spinner above to make the three sectors the approximate size you would expect them to be. Label them orange, purple, and green.

descriptors: Orange sector approximately half the circle, green and purple each approximately one-quarter, all correctly labeled
Only one labeled sector the correct size
Three sectors drawn but none the correct size
Three sectors of correct size drawn but no labels
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

Around the circumference of the circle is an outer rim with 8 equally spaced tick marks, dividing the circle into 8 equal arcs of 45° each (at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30). The interior of the circle is blank.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D]

Continue to identify the tiles as shown above. On the grid below, write the letters A, B, C, or D to make a symmetrical pattern where PQ and RS would be lines of symmetry. Arrange the tiles to make a pattern.

[Image: A 4 by 4 grid with axes PQ and RS]

descriptors: All cells are correct with symmetrical geometric pattern about both axes, PQ and RS (letters or drawings).
With respect to at least one of the original tiles the other three tiles are correct.
Letters placed symmetrically with respect to both PQ and RS.
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task).

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D are shown in a row. Each tile is divided conceptually into four smaller quadrants:
- Tile A: A shaded black triangle in the upper-left corner (formed by the diagonal connecting the midpoint of the top edge and the midpoint of the left edge) and a solid black square in the lower-right quadrant.
- Tile B: A shaded black triangle in the upper-right corner and a solid black square in the lower-left quadrant.
- Tile C: A solid black square in the upper-left quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-right corner.
- Tile D: A solid black square in the upper-right quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-left corner.

Below is a 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line PQ and a horizontal line RS. P is at the top of the vertical line, Q is at the bottom; R is at the left of the horizontal line, S is at the right. Four squares are already labeled:
- Row 1 (top), column 1 (left): 'D'
- Row 2, column 4 (right): 'C'
- Row 3, column 2: 'B'
- Row 4 (bottom), column 3: 'A'
The remaining 12 squares are blank.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
